questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How robots will replace people in the home
Why science-fiction novels are popular again
How much smart devices cost to buy
Whether smart technology can help fight climate change
questions.why: Neil says some people are wondering whether smart tech can help fight climate change.

questions.q: How can a smart home help save resources, according to Sam?
options: By turning off all devices automatically every night
By learning when people are home and heating at the best time
By producing its own electricity from solar panels on the roof
By reminding people to buy fewer devices for their home
questions.why: Sam says AI can learn when the house is occupied and the best time to turn on the heating.

questions.q: What problem does Neil point out with smart home systems?
options: The energy that powers them may come from fossil fuels
They break down too easily
They are too difficult for older people to use
They collect too much personal information
questions.why: Neil says the problem is the origin of the energy: if it's fossil fuels, burning them creates emissions.

questions.q: What is Dr Enass Abo-Hamed testing on Orkney?
options: New kinds of wind turbines
Smart lights for island homes
Ways to store renewable energy
Ways to dig up fossil fuels more safely
questions.why: She is working on a project on Orkney testing ways of storing renewable energy.

questions.q: Why does Dr Abo-Hamed say renewable energy is not always reliable?
options: Because the equipment is very old
Because it is too expensive for most countries
Because people don't want to use it
Because it depends on the sun and the wind
questions.why: She says it relies on the weather – when the sun shines and the wind blows.

questions.q: What happens when a lot of renewable power is produced but nobody needs it?
options: The energy is wasted
There is a blackout
The price of electricity goes up
It is sent to other countries
questions.why: She says when there's no demand for the power, 'it's wasted'.

questions.q: What is a 'digital twin', as Graihagh Jackson describes it?
options: A second wind turbine built next to the first as a backup
A computer model of a turbine using live sensor data
An engineer who checks turbines at sea in bad weather
A smart device that controls the heating in two homes at once
questions.why: Sensors are attached to the turbine so it can be modelled on a computer in real time.

questions.q: Why does Graihagh Jackson think digital twins are important?
options: They make wind turbines much cheaper to build and transport
They stop turbines from making noise near people's homes
They help make sure turbines work as well as possible
They replace the need for engineers to visit the turbines
questions.why: She says they can make sure the turbines are 'performing their best'.
